newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian rail unions call off protests over safety.
newsitem.headline: Italian rail unions call off protests over safety.

text.p: Rail traffic in Italy returned to normal on Tuesday when unions called off protests which had disrupted service after the state railway agreed to review safety procedures following a fatal derailment.
Trains on Monday were delayed up to an hour when train drivers staged a go-slow protest in which they kept to speeds below the limits set out for various sections of track.

The drivers' action and another strike planned for this week by station employees, who control the flow of rail traffic, had been called by unions to demand a safety review after the derailment of a high-speed train on January 12 which killed eight people.
The unions cancelled the protests on Monday evening after they said their demands were met at talks with Transport Minister Claudio Burlando and representatives of the railway, Ferrovie dello Stato.
The railway said the agreement reinforced already established safety procedures.
